thread:
Kai (Growth): Hey team — after last night's partial region degradation I want to lock down the customer-facing cadence. I sketched a phased update checklist, need input on tone + routing.
Maria (Comms): Thanks Kai. Can you drop the checklist here? I'll riff on language for EU vs NA.
Kai (Growth): Pasting a compact checklist, high level then templates below. Please comment inline.
Oliver (Product Marketing): Quick ask: include a short bench narrative paragraph for customers worried about SLA/credits.
Sara (Support Lead): Also we need an inbound routing rule so high-value accounts hit Sales Ops and Tier 2 immediately.
Jamal (SRE): FYI: root cause is a networking flake in eu-west, mitigation is live but we're watching. ETA for normal ops ~3 hours.
Maria (Comms): Ok suggested timing: initial notice at T=0 (alert with impact + workaround), T+30m short update, T+2h technical update (if available), T+4h recovery/next steps. If we're confident earlier, compress. Keep customer-facing language calm.
Kai (Growth): Routing: public status page + email to all customers for major incidents; targeted email to dedicated/dedicated+private customers with SLA language; and slack/webhook to partner integrators.
Oliver (Product Marketing): Bench narrative: "We prioritize availability and have preserved state for all in-flight requests; we're issuing credits for any SLA shortfall while we complete recovery." Short and actionable.
Maria (Comms): Tone snippets: 1) High-level: "We are aware of an incident affecting inference in eu-west. Our engineers are working on a fix." 2) Technical: "The issue originated in network fabric causing elevated latency and tail errors for a subset of GPU hosts." 3) Recovery: "Services have been restored; we continue to monitor and will publish a post-incident summary." Pick versions based on audience.
Sara (Support Lead): Routing rule for high-value inbound: if account_tier in (enterprise, dedicated) OR monthly_spend > 10k -> create ticket with label #priority-sales, notify Jamal + Maria + Assigned AE. Can product/engineering provide account list?
Kai (Growth): I'll export a list and drop in the shared drive.
Jamal (SRE): For status page copy here's a short template we can use. Please sanity-check:
status-bot: "[Automatically formatted preview]
- Impact: Partial service interruption for inference requests routed to eu-west.
- Scope: Approximately X% of requests experienced increased latency or errors between 02:10-02:40 UTC.
- Mitigation: Traffic was shifted and retries implemented; engineering applied a network config change at 03:05 UTC.
- Action: We are monitoring; next update in 30 minutes or when a significant change occurs."
Maria (Comms): Nice. For the public status page I'd tweak to remove % if uncertain: "a subset of requests experienced..." and add "Workaround: automatic retries applied by our routing layer."
Oliver (Product Marketing): For webinar registrants (we have a webinar in 48h) we should send a short note: "We've experienced a transient issue; platform is recovering and the webinar will proceed as scheduled. If anything changes we'll notify registrants and offer reschedule options." Keep it empathetic.
Sara (Support Lead): Suggest canned support replies for Tier 1: short, what happened, ETA, workaround, link to status page, contact escalation path. Example: "Thanks for flagging — we’re aware of a transient issue impacting inference in eu-west. Our SREs are working on it; estimated resolution ~3 hours. Please retry; if you see persistent failures open a ticket and we'll escalate."
Maria (Comms): Translation checklist: prioritize ES, FR, DE for major incidents (EU-heavy). Use plain language, avoid technical verbs that confuse. I can own translations if we get final copy.
Kai (Growth): A/B test note: Post-incident, let's try two subject lines for the follow-up email for churn risk customers: 1) "Incident resolved — summary + credits" vs 2) "How we prevented recurrence — post-incident summary" — track open rates and escalation tickets.
Jamal (SRE): One safety ask: if we plan to mention credits publicly, ping finance to confirm thresholds.
Oliver (Product Marketing): Also recommend adding a short FAQ snippet on the status page: "Will I be charged?" -> "We will assess any SLA impact and notify affected customers about credits or adjustments."
Maria (Comms): Timeline action items: 
- T0: Maria publishes status page + email to all customers (public language).
- T0+15: Sara posts canned support replies & routes top-tier tickets.
- T+30: Jamal provides technical update for status page and targeted email to dedicated customers.
- T+2h: Maria drafts recovery + postmortem placeholder and schedules post for 24–48h.
- Postmortem: official long-form RCA + bench narrative + mitigation plan.
Kai (Growth): Who owns what: Maria = comms + translations; Sara = support routing + canned replies; Jamal = technical updates; Oliver = bench narrative & webinar registrant message; Kai = priority account list & A/B test config.
Maria (Comms): I'll assemble the actual copy blocks now. Dropping first-pass templates:
---
Public status snippet: "We are aware of an issue affecting inference in eu-west. Some requests may see increased latency or errors. Our engineers have applied mitigations and we are monitoring. For status and updates: <status.redwood.ai>"
Dedicated customer snippet: "We are experiencing partial service degradation in eu-west affecting a subset of requests. Our engineering team implemented a mitigation at 03:05 UTC and is monitoring. If you depend on reserved capacity, please contact your account team for assistance and temporary failover options."
Support canned reply (short): "Hi — thanks for reporting. We’re aware of an incident affecting eu-west inference. Engineers are working on a fix; estimated time to recovery ~3 hours. Please retry and let us know if failures persist. Status updates: <status.redwood.ai>"
---
Sara (Support Lead): These look good. I'll paste them into Helpdesk macro set now.
Maria (Comms): One more: social post for X/LinkedIn (short): "We're investigating a service disruption in eu-west affecting inference latency. Our engineers are on it and we've applied mitigations. Status updates: <status.redwood.ai>"
Oliver (Product Marketing): For the bench narrative paragraph to include in postmortem: "During the incident we prioritized state preservation and customer traffic routing. While a subset of requests saw increased latency, caching and prefix replay limited customer-visible regressions. We are issuing credits where SLA thresholds were not met and will publish additional guidance for on-prem/private customers."
Kai (Growth): Great sync. Any blockers on approvals? Finance for credits, legal for language about SLA. Maria — can you get both looped?
Maria (Comms): Yes, I'll loop finance + legal now. Paging @finance, @legal in the thread.
status-bot: "Finance team paged: ticket #INC-2026-331 created for credit threshold approval."
Kai (Growth): Thanks. Let's keep updates terse in this channel — I'll post the finalized templates after approvals. :thumbsup:
Maria (Comms): Will do. I'll post final versions into #ops-marketing-assets and notify product docs for the postmortem link.
Sara (Support Lead): Done on macros. Will escalate any priority inbound immediately.
Jamal (SRE): Monitoring. I'll update at T+30.
Maria (Comms): Closing loop — final note: keep one canonical status page and link everything to it. Avoid duplicative emails unless targeted to SLA customers.
Kai (Growth): Agreed. Thanks everyone.
